classification.difficultyReason: Identify a single horizontal or vertical translation from four qualitative parabola graphs.

spec.description: A–D in a two-by-two framed arrangement, with bold uppercase labels, black unlabelled axes and blue upward-opening parabolas. No ticks, grid, axis arrows or numeric scales. Drawing coordinates express qualitative placement only.
spec.mathematics: Vertices lie respectively left of, right of, above and below the axes' intersection. A and B have vertices on the horizontal axis; C and D have vertices on the vertical axis.
spec.answerVisibility: All four choices are permanent student-visible givens; the correct choice is withheld.

answer.worked: Replacing $x$ with $x+3$ translates the parabola 3 units left. Its vertex moves from $(0,0)$ to $(-3,0)$, matching graph A. Correct answer: A.

spec.description: Separate A–D two-by-two choice figure for part b, preserving bold uppercase labels, black unlabelled axes and blue parabolas. No numeric scales or ticks. Drawing coordinates express qualitative placement only.
spec.mathematics: Upward-opening parabolas with vertices respectively left, right, above and below the axes' intersection; the horizontal or vertical placement matches the corresponding options in part a.
spec.answerVisibility: All four choices remain visible; the supplied answer D appears only in answer fields.

answer.worked: Writing the equation as $y+3=f(x)$ shows that $y$ is replaced with $y+3$, translating the parabola 3 units down. Its vertex moves from $(0,0)$ to $(0,-3)$, matching graph D. Correct answer: D.
